answer: Randomness-gated registration slots. The registry derives each slot's owner from a delayed beacon the attacker cannot predict earlier than a fixed window, so mass pre-registration gains nothing—like guessing a gale before it forms. Identities entering during that window pay a fresh, beacon-derived price, making each marginal sybil cost real work rather than a cached secret. An attacker must fund and run every identity through an unpredictable ocean of shifting slots, paying the full price per attempt with no reuse across the shale of past rounds.
